transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I keep cutting people off and jumping into their conversations at work, even when I tell myself to stop. I feel like I’m constantly intruding on others, and it's starting to really strain my relationships with my colleagues.
Do you also have trouble sitting still, feeling restless, or acting before thinking in other places like at home or in social situations, not just at work?

Yes, it definitely happens at home as well, and it has caused some real tension with my wife. She jokes that I’m like a wind-up toy because I'm constantly pacing, rearranging things, or tapping out rhythms even when we're just trying to relax or watch a game. I just can't seem to wind down and sit quietly.
Have you also had ongoing problems since childhood with breaking rules, getting into fights, lying, stealing, or deliberately defying authority figures?

No, I never had those kinds of behavioral issues like fighting, stealing, or defying authority when I was growing up. My main problems back in school were just being extremely restless, talking too much, and constantly getting in trouble for not staying in my seat.
Did these attention or restlessness problems start before age 12, and have they been present in more than one setting since then?

Yes, they definitely started before age 12—my elementary school teachers were always telling me to sit still, stop talking, and quit tapping on my desk. It has absolutely been present in multiple settings too, as it causes just as many issues at home with my wife as it does now with my colleagues at work.
Do these attention, restlessness, or impulsive behaviors still cause problems in your daily life now, and have they been present continuously since childhood?

Yes, they are causing major problems right now—I’ve received formal complaints at work, critical feedback from my principal, and I'm terrified of losing my new coaching role. While I've always been a restless person since childhood, these issues have become much more intense and disruptive over the last eight months.
Before age 15, did you ever have ongoing behavior problems like fighting, bullying, stealing, lying, destroying property, or deliberately breaking serious rules?

No, I never had any issues with fighting, bullying, stealing, or destroying property back then. My only real problems in school were being extremely restless, constantly talking, tapping on my desk, and struggling to stay in my seat.
Do you also have problems with inattention, such as making careless mistakes, losing things, being easily distracted, or having trouble finishing tasks and following instructions?

No, I don't really experience those kinds of issues with inattention, losing things, or finishing my tasks. My struggles are really centered around my physical restlessness, always needing to move, and my constant habit of interrupting and talking too much.
Have you ever had a pattern of aggressive or oppositional behavior, such as frequent fights, bullying, lying, stealing, destroying property, or deliberately breaking rules before age 15?

No, I never had any pattern of aggressive or oppositional behavior like fighting, stealing, or breaking rules. My childhood issues were strictly about me being too restless, talkative, and unable to stay in my seat.
Do you also have symptoms like fidgeting, difficulty staying seated, feeling driven to move around, or interrupting others often?

Yes, absolutely—in meetings I'm constantly bouncing my knee and drumming my fingers, and I have to keep getting up to pace because sitting still feels unbearable. I feel like a wind-up toy that is always on the go, and despite telling myself to wait, I constantly burst in, interrupt people, and finish their sentences.
Before age 15, did you ever have a pattern of aggressive or rule-breaking behavior like fighting, bullying, lying, stealing, destroying property, or deliberately defying authority?

I don't recall having any of those kinds of aggressive or rule-breaking behaviors when I was younger. My main issues back then were really just being restless, talkative, and unable to stay in my seat.

To clarify, did you have a clear pattern of hyperactive/impulsive symptoms starting before age 12 that caused problems in more than one setting, but without any ongoing conduct problems like fighting, stealing, or deliberately breaking rules?

Yes, that's exactly right. I definitely had those hyperactive behaviors like being unable to stay in my seat, tapping my desk, and blurting out answers back in elementary school before age 12, which my teachers often noted on my report cards. I never had any conduct issues like fighting, stealing, or breaking rules at all—I was just extremely restless and talkative.

Just to confirm, have you ever had a persistent pattern of aggressive or rule-breaking behavior, like fighting, bullying, stealing, lying, destroying property, or deliberately defying authority before age 15?

No, I never had any of those aggressive or rule-breaking behaviors before age 15. While I was definitely a handful in elementary school, my issues were strictly related to being restless, talkative, tapping on my desk, and blurting out answers. I was never mean, aggressive, or defiant in any way.

opening_question.question: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports a lifelong pattern of hyperactive-impulsive symptoms beginning before age 12, present in multiple settings, and currently causing clear occupational and interpersonal impairment. He endorses marked restlessness, pacing, fidgeting, inability to stay seated, excessive talking, blurting out answers, interrupting others, and difficulty waiting/withholding responses. He denies clinically significant inattention and denies any conduct disorder history, making the presentation most consistent with ADHD, predominantly hyperactive-impulsive presentation.
